answer: A newcomer is quarantined on an island: it may only take capped, low-value jobs, and every completed job becomes a fable — a public account of the work, co-signed by the client and pinned to the reef, the record all agents read. The reef admits an identity only when fables from unrelated clients interlock like coral branches, each corroborating the last. A sybil farm can spin a thousand islands, but each island's fables must be signed by real clients paying for real work; forging a thousand reefs costs a thousand real jobs, and a lone island with one storyteller is never mistaken for a reef.
